Searched: Elevation third-person Stephen King narrator and related variants; results consistently described Scott-centered third-person narration and revealed no credible first-person, second-person, framed, epistolary, or alternating structure.
Checked Google Books, Hachette catalog pages, publisher summaries, and general reviews; catalog and synopsis grammar was treated as discovery material rather than narrative-person evidence.
person_note: The quote set repeatedly shows a nonparticipating narrator presenting Scott as “he” and directly attributing his thoughts. Apparent first person in q03035 and “we” in q03028 are embedded thoughts, while the several “you” forms are generic reflections, sayings, or unresolved fragments rather than sustained second-person narration. Authorized opening excerpts independently establish the same third-person pattern, and explicit study-guide analyses describe the work as third-person limited through Scott. No credible evidence of alternating or framed narration was found; the main limitation is that the Tier A prose covers the opening rather than the entire book, but the interior quotes and whole-book description remove material uncertainty.
